prompt: Which relationship between the nuclear envelope and ER is correct?

options.text: The outer nuclear membrane is continuous with rough ER and may bear ribosomes
The inner nuclear membrane is continuous with Golgi cisternae
Both membranes are isolated from all endomembranes
The perinuclear space is the mitochondrial matrix

explanation: The outer nuclear membrane continues into RER, and the perinuclear space is continuous with the ER lumen; the inner membrane associates with lamina and chromatin.

distractorExplanations.B: The inner membrane is supported by nuclear lamina, not Golgi continuity.
distractorExplanations.C: The envelope is part of the endomembrane system.
distractorExplanations.D: Perinuclear space is continuous with ER lumen, not mitochondrial matrix.

learningObjective: Describe nuclear-envelope continuity and membrane specialization.

subject: histology
prompt: A large intensely basophilic nucleolus indicates high activity in which process?
explanation: Dense rRNA and associated proteins make the nucleolus basophilic; it transcribes/processes rRNA and assembles ribosomal subunits.

distractorExplanations.B: Beta-oxidation is mitochondrial/peroxisomal.
distractorExplanations.C: Clathrin budding occurs at membranes.
distractorExplanations.D: Collagen synthesis uses RER/Golgi; nucleolar enlargement reflects ribosome production indirectly.

learningObjective: Relate nucleolar basophilia to ribosome biogenesis.

source.lecture: Dr Tayebeh Rastegar, Anatomy Department, TUMS
source.excerpt: Nucleolus is highly basophilic because of concentrated rRNA.

subject: histology
prompt: Which observation favors apoptosis over necrosis?

options.text: Cell shrinkage, membrane blebs and apoptotic bodies with limited inflammation
Early plasma-membrane rupture and tissue inflammation
Cell swelling with uncontrolled enzyme leakage

explanation: Apoptosis is a caspase-driven, orderly process with cell shrinkage, chromatin condensation, blebbing and phagocytosis of membrane-bound fragments.

distractorExplanations.B: Membrane rupture and inflammation favor necrosis.
distractorExplanations.C: Swelling and leakage favor necrosis.
distractorExplanations.D: Apoptosis is cell-autonomous and limits bystander injury.

learningObjective: Distinguish morphologic consequences of apoptosis and necrosis.

subject: histology
prompt: A mitotic cell has sister chromatids moving toward opposite poles after centromere division. Which stage is it in?
explanation: Anaphase begins when centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite spindle poles.

distractorExplanations.B: Prophase features chromosome condensation and spindle formation.
distractorExplanations.C: Metaphase aligns duplicated chromosomes at the equator.
distractorExplanations.D: Telophase re-forms nuclei around separated chromosomes.

learningObjective: Identify anaphase from chromatid separation.

source.lecture: Dr Tayebeh Rastegar, Anatomy Department, TUMS

subject: histology
prompt: Which event occurs before meiosis I but not between meiosis I and meiosis II?
explanation: DNA replicates once before meiosis I. There is no second S phase before meiosis II, when sister chromatids separate.

distractorExplanations.B: Chromatids separate in meiosis II.
distractorExplanations.C: Spindles form in both divisions.
distractorExplanations.D: Chromosomes condense in both divisions.

learningObjective: Explain the single replication followed by two meiotic divisions.

source.title: lecture 1 .pptx
source.lecture: Dr Tayebeh Rastegar, Anatomy Department, TUMS
source.excerpt: Meiosis I follows DNA replication; meiosis II has no further DNA replication.

subject: histology
prompt: Which reaction is most characteristic of peroxisomes in the teacher lecture?

options.text: Oxidases generate H2O2 and catalase converts it to water and oxygen
Ribosomes synthesize secretory proteins into cisternae
ATP synthase uses a proton gradient on cristae

explanation: Peroxisomal oxidases remove hydrogen and form H2O2; catalase safely decomposes it. Peroxisomes also participate in lipid metabolism and very-long-chain fatty-acid oxidation.

distractorExplanations.B: That is lysosomal digestion.
distractorExplanations.C: That is RER protein synthesis.
distractorExplanations.D: That is mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation.

learningObjective: Differentiate peroxisomal oxidation/catalase from lysosomal and mitochondrial functions.
